solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of bedroom set from Knickerbox

definitions.meaning: a piece of bedroom furniture from a matching suite
read literally, a box for knickers, which old-fashioned British English also calls drawers

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a bedroom item from Knickerbox, a British lingerie chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Knickerbox is the name of a UK lingerie retailer, which hides the literal reading: a box (chest) holding drawers, an old word for knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall piece of furniture with sliding compartments is a standard item in a matching bedroom suite.

clue.text: Unfashionable hire shop?

parts.note: something unfashionable is out
to let a property is to hire it out

explanation.surface: A clothes-hire business that has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose one: a retail outlet is a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory or retail outlet is a store selling goods, so it fits a shop by example.

clue.text: Short tune by one playing instrument

indicators.note: short means the word for tune loses its last letter

parts.note: a tune is a melody

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of one are performing about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician plays a brief tune alongside someone else performing on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like part of the musical picture but signals that the three letters of 'one' are rearranged; 'Short' trims the final letter of the tune word.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodeon is a small accordion or reed organ, a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Compass point briefly shown by the needle

definitions.text: Compass point briefly shown by the needle

parts.words: Compass point briefly shown by the needle
parts.note: the compass direction whose short form, ENE, sits in the letters of thE NEedle, while a compass needle seems to be pointing

explanation.surface: A compass needle points to a direction on the dial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' asks for the abbreviation ENE, and 'shown by' finds it spelt across thE NEedle; the full direction is the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearing between east and northeast is one of the sixteen named points of the compass rose.

clue.text: International organisation initially comes up short, needing enhanced overseas supply

indicators.note: supply read as supple-ly, in a flexible manner, so those initial letters are rearranged
initially says take the opening letter of each of the six words that follow

explanation.surface: An aid body falls short and needs more supplies sent overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, not the noun, so it rearranges CUSNEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization is a worldwide UN agency.

clue.text: Punctilious poet's raised foot above head in photo

indicators.note: in puts the reshaped poet inside the word for photo

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of the poet's name is lifted to sit above its head, moving the last letter to the front

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fussy poet's photograph shows his foot raised over his head.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised foot above head' lifts the poet's last letter to the top, and 'in' splits the photo word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punctilious is exacting over small details, as a pedantic person is.

clue.text: Doctor injecting poet with drug

indicators.note: injecting means the drug goes inside the poet's name

parts.note: A. E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a poet an injection of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is the British term for a junior hospital doctor in the first year after qualifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior hospital physician in Britain is called a houseman, so the title names a doctor.

clue.text: Plan made by Home Guard

parts.note: at home is in
to tend is to look after or guard

explanation.surface: A wartime plan drawn up by the Home Guard, Britain's WWII volunteer defence force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer local defence force in the Second World War; here the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to have it in mind as a purpose, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Eat indoors? Tin is opened drunkedly, showing confusion regarding directions

indicators.note: drunkedly, written that way by the setter, means unsteadily, so the letters reel about
opened means only the opening letter of is is used

explanation.surface: Someone eats inside, opens a tin while tipsy, and loses their bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' gives just I from 'is', which joins EATINDOORS and TIN before 'drunkedly' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing your sense of which way is which is exactly being confused about directions.

clue.text: Awfully cold April — start of Ice Age?

definitions.text: Awfully cold April — start of Ice Age?

indicators.note: awfully suggests things are badly arranged, so the letters are rearranged
start of takes only the opening letter of ice

explanation.surface: A dreadfully cold April makes someone wonder if an ice age is starting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the fodder and a playful description: a freezing spell that might mark the beginning of a frozen era.
explanation.definitionFit: A long era of ice sheets spreading, the start of which a bitterly cold spring might jokingly suggest.

clue.text: Saudi Arabia lost 5-0 due to sudden burst of shooting

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost in sports results
five is V in Roman numerals and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: A football report: Saudi Arabia lost five-nil after a sudden flurry of shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The score reads as football but gives Roman V and the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a sudden burst of firing.

clue.text: Left Italy, seduced by navigator's charms

indicators.note: being seduced by someone means being taken in by them, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Someone left Italy, won over by a sailor's charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seduced by' puts L and I inside TASMANS, the possessive giving the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky charms and amulets believed to bring good fortune are talismans.

clue.text: Very busy month, eg October to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: October is described as a hectic month.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in mONTH and finishes in EG and the O of October.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly active and rushing about is an idiom for being very busy.

clue.text: One farming a small area is frequently in credit, after 50% taken off starting rent

indicators.note: in places the word for frequently inside the shortened credit
in places the word for frequently inside the shortened credit
half the letters of credit are removed, keeping the first three

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently

indicators.note: starting takes the opening letter of rent

explanation.surface: A smallholder is often in the black once half the first rent payment is knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% taken off' leaves CRE of CREDIT, into which OFT goes, then R from 'starting rent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter works a croft, a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands and Islands.

clue.text: The CID inter a leftie criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests a crooked state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Detectives from the CID bury a left-wing criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like the start of the sentence but is the whole definition. CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the word 'the' is the English determiner marking a specific noun, the definite article.

clue.text: Giving up strong drink, drinks nothing during endless orgy

parts.note: F is forte, the musical mark for loud and strong

indicators.note: during places the drinking piece inside the shortened orgy
endless removes the final letter of orgy

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: the spirit drinks, taking the zero letter inside itself

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a strong drink
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone abstains from spirits, drinking nothing during a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' puts O into GIN for GOIN; 'during' places that inside ORG from 'endless orgy', all after F.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without, so going without something is giving it up.

clue.text: Lead must be taken off dog when inside as well, it's so long

indicators.note: the trimmed dog sits inside the word for as well

parts.note: too means as well, also

indicators.note: the first letter of the dog's name is removed, a lead being what it wears at the front

parts.note: a poodle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dog-owner: unclip the lead indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a dog's leash but means the leading letter; 'when inside' splits the word for as well after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty dated British way of saying goodbye, as is the phrase so long.

clue.text: Golden labrador's head, to right of the external ear

parts.note: auric means of or like gold

indicators.note: head takes the opening letter of labrador
the rightmost letter of the word the is taken

explanation.surface: A golden labrador's head is described down to the outer ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden labrador' reads as the dog breed, but splits into AURIC and L; 'to right of the' gives E, the right-hand end of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the visible flap of the outer ear is called the auricle or pinna.

clue.text: During broadcast, see you cook game bird

indicators.note: broadcast says the words are said out loud, so see you gives the two letters it sounds like

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like CU

indicators.note: game in the sense of lame or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV chef tells viewers to see them when they cook a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' wants to be the definition; 'game' is the anagram signal turning COOK into KOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuckoo is a European bird famous for its call and for laying eggs in other nests.

clue.text: Predictor of future Hungary to Japan switch for aeroplane

indicators.note: switch says one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: a prophet predicts the future
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

explanation.surface: A seer predicts a shift from Hungary to Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hungary to Japan switch' swaps the H of PROPHET for J.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop airliner, driven by a jet engine turning propellers, is a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Setter goes on vacation, getting to talk about puzzle

indicators.note: about means the talk piece wraps around the others

parts.note: to jaw is to chatter, talk at length
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: on vacation means the word is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter goes on holiday and gets chatting about a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties a word of its contents, a common crossword trick; 'Setter' is the compiler speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture cut into interlocking pieces to reassemble is a classic puzzle.

clue.text: One that drives out from Gold Coast's first to wear sexier pants

indicators.note: the pieces wear the rearranged word, so they go inside it
pants is slang for rubbish, so the word is messed up

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Coast

explanation.surface: Someone from Australia's Gold Coast is the first to wear racier underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but rearranges SEXIER to EXISER, which takes in OR and C; the Gold Coast is a Queensland resort city.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist casts out evil spirits, so is one who drives them out.

clue.text: It's not against the law to run away

explanation.surface: Running off isn't actually illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the two-word phrase LEG IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for legitimate, slang for lawful; and the phrase for bolting means running away.

clue.text: Fourth-year student back home in south-eastern Oregon

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the others

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for Oregon

indicators.note: back says the word for home is turned round

parts.note: at home is in

explanation.surface: A final-year student heads back home to south-east Oregon.
explanation.walkthrough: In a US four-year college the final-year student is a senior.
explanation.definitionFit: American high schools and colleges call fourth-year students seniors.

clue.text: State of Wisconsin's just left of centre

definitions.text: State of Wisconsin's just left of centre

parts.words: State of Wisconsin's just left of centre
parts.note: the centre letter of Wisconsin is O, and the pair ending there, just left of centre, is CO, the postal code of a western US state

explanation.surface: A remark on US geography: a state lies a little west of the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The state is reached through its abbreviation CO, spelt by the fourth and fifth letters of WISCONSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rocky Mountain state of the western US, whose two-letter abbreviation is CO.
